To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GSK3 inhibits HSF1 DNA binding and transcriptional activities in vivo during heat shock.
GSK3 inhibits both DNA binding and transcription of HSF1 and that GSK3 regulates HSF1 activity during both heat shock and recovery.
GSK3 negatively regulates both DNA binding and transcriptional activities in HSF1 in cells during heat stress and recovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Gsk3b in the regulation of HSF1 DNA binding and transcriptional activation during stress.
the regulation of the stress-inducible transcription factor heat shock factor ( HSF ) by glycogen synthetase kinase (Gsk) 3β in heat-shocked mammalian cells.
understanding the molecular mechanisms by which GSK3β regulates HSF1 activity and the role of GSF3β in heat shock responses in cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GSK3 negatively regulates HSF1 by inhibiting both DNA binding and transactivation activities.
GSK3 inhibits both DNA binding and transcriptional activities in HSF1.
GSK3 is a negative regulator of the HSF1 pathway and that this is due to both transcriptional repression and DNA binding inhibition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSF1 activity is regulated by the balance of positive and negative signals, including the activity of GSK3, that control the ability of the HSF1 trimer to interact with the heat shock promoter.
GSK3 negatively regulates HSF1 by phosphorylating Ser230, which is required for HSF1 DNA binding.
GSK3 is an important negative regulator of Hsp transcription and that it functions to repress HSF DNA-binding activity in vivo during heat shock.

the regulation of DNA binding is an essential part of GSK3's ability to control HSF1 activity.
